#4948. The 1Password Breach Didn’t Touch Your Vault. The Phishing Emails Might

The 1Password Breach Didn’t Touch Your Vault. The Phishing Emails Might

Password manager 1Password has disclosed a security breach in which an attacker accessed some of its backend systems and copied customer account information, though the company says the vaults where users store their passwords and other secrets were never touched.

In a disclosure published Tuesday, the Toronto-based firm said it began investigating on Nov. 19 after detecting that an attacker had gained access to an employee’s corporate GitHub account. The intruder used that access to reach

1Password’s source code and push malicious code to backend services, which then downloaded administrative data on a subset of customers. At no point, the company said, were vault contents accessible to the attacker.

Here’s what was taken, according to 1Password: customer names and email addresses, account and user identifiers, account creation and last sign-in times, public keys (which are public by design), certain protocol parameters that can’t be used to access an account, and non-secret internal metadata.

The attacker also copied source code from private repositories and gained access to the company’s software build systems, which hold some infrastructure credentials. 1Password said it has rotated all credentials that may have been exposed.

Crucially for users, the breach did not expose the data that actually matters: your vaults, the items inside them, the keys that protect them, or your account recovery keys.

1Password’s design means it never stores your account password or Secret Key, so an attacker who gets into its servers still can’t decrypt your vault. The company stressed there’s nothing you need to change in your account, and its apps and browser extensions are working normally.

What users should do, for now, comes down to what is generally good advice at all times: watch out for phishing emails, because they’re surely coming.

Because names and email addresses were exposed, affected users are prime targets for scam emails impersonating 1Password, particularly fake account-recovery or invitation requests.

The company urged caution with any unexpected message mentioning 1Password, and reiterated that it will never contact you to ask for your account password or Secret Key, which you should only ever enter in the official app or on the official site after opening it yourself.

One wrinkle involves emailed invitation and recovery links, which contain a token. 1Password said a small number of users in that state were notified directly; as a precaution, it lengthened the verification codes in those emails from six digits to ten alphanumeric characters to make guessing them impractical.

The incident echoes a run of breaches hitting companies that hold users’ most sensitive data, a pattern that has emerged this year as attackers increasingly target third-party systems and developer accounts rather than the encryption itself.

#4946. Binance Fully Lifts Withdrawal Suspension a Month After $6.3 Billion Hack

Binance has fully lifted the withdrawal suspension it put in place after last month’s record $6.3 billion hack, saying its recovery work is complete and that withdrawals are open across nearly all networks.

“Our withdrawal recovery work is completed and the withdrawal suspension from the security incident has been fully lifted,” the exchange said in an X post Thursday afternoon. A small number of networks remain paused for maintenance, which Binance called standard practice and said was unrelated to the hack.

The update closes out a month of phased reopenings. Binance confirmed the breach on Oct. 29, saying its initial investigation pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop that gave the attacker access to a service container, which was then used to submit unauthorized withdrawals.

The world’s largest crypto exchange stopped all customer withdrawals for two days after the theft, Reuters reported. When they first reopened, customers pulled a net $4.7 billion off the platform, Binance said on Nov. 2.

Binance said on Nov. 12 that it had completed coverage of the affected assets with more than $6.34 billion of company funds. The money came from a partial draw on its Secure Asset Fund for Users, part of its futures insurance fund and its corporate treasury, and the exchange pledged to rebuild SAFU to about $1 billion.

Coverage is not the same as recovery. Binance replaced the stolen tokens from its own books, while about $2.85 billion of the stolen funds have been frozen remotely by the companies that issue them. The rest remains in the hands of the attackers.

U.S. authorities have blamed North Korean hackers for the theft, which North Korea denies. On Nov. 23, the Justice Department moved to forfeit more than $1.1 billion in USDC that Circle froze, and said the U.S. has helped freeze, seize or return more than $2.9 billion since the attack.

The unfrozen funds are on the move. North Korean launderers have stepped up transfers through THORChain and a coinjoin service in recent days, blockchain researchers told Reuters, as part of an operation spanning tens of thousands of transactions across blockchains.

Chainalysis and Elliptic estimate that more than $600 million of the stolen crypto has passed through THORChain, though Elliptic said that figure could count funds that went through more than once. TRM Labs estimates THORChain earned as much as $1 million in fees from the swaps.

Separately, $342 million has moved through a coinjoin service mostly coordinated by a pseudonymous figure named Kruw, Elliptic said. A coinjoin combines coins from many users into a single transaction, so their origin is no longer visible on the blockchain. Elliptic has said the launderers will still need other services, such as over-the-counter brokers, to turn the coins into cash.

The FBI on Oct. 31 published wallet addresses used by the attacker and asked crypto service providers, including the network of computers that runs THORChain, to block them. In a video posted Thursday, THORChain co-founder Chad Barraford said 98% of trading on the network was for people’s “own individual financial freedom and liberty.”

THORChain, which describes itself as decentralized, says on its website that it does not “censor” transactions or run Know-Your-Customer checks. Ari Redbord, global head of policy at TRM Labs, called the FBI’s move to single out the network’s operators “pretty extraordinary.”

Redbord said the laundering could take months or even years, and that cashing out even a fraction would be a windfall for North Korea. The total stolen from Binance equals about a sixth of the country’s estimated gross domestic product.

“They don’t have to get a lot off in order to make this all worthwhile for them,” Redbord said.

#4942. What Happened to Alice Huang, the Woman at the Center of Nvidia’s Scandal?

What Happened to Alice Huang, the Woman at the Center of Nvidia’s Scandal?

While Jensen Huang has returned to the helm of Nvidia following a brief but dramatic departure, the Chinese businesswoman at the center of the scandal that threatened his career remains largely out of public view.

U.S. intelligence officials told congressional staffers on Tuesday that they had found no evidence that Alice Huang was instructed by Chinese intelligence to spy on the Nvidia chief executive, The Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday, citing people familiar with the classified briefing.

Although officials claimed that she had contacted China's intelligence service during the affair, they found no indication that she had passed on significant intelligence. The assessment could change if new evidence emerges.

You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Nvidia with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.

The findings mark a significant development in a controversy that has shaken Silicon Valley—and the whole global economy alongside it—and heightened tensions over China's access to advanced American technology.

But for Alice Huang, questions surrounding her business activities, legal situation and future remain unresolved.

Also known by her Chinese name, Huang Le, Alice Huang is a Hong Kong resident who previously led Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based cloud computing company that became a major customer of Nvidia.

The company originated as the overseas subsidiary of a Chinese video game business before shifting into artificial intelligence infrastructure. It became an official Nvidia cloud partner in November 2023.

According to corporate records cited by the Associated Press, Huang ceased to be a registered director of Megaspeed in November 2023, although Singaporean authorities identified her as its chief executive, chairperson and a key controller when they investigated the company in 2025.

Megaspeed said on November 15 that Huang had formally departed on August 30, 2025, and no longer held any position within the company. It declined to discuss her private affairs and maintained that its business operations were lawful.

Huang's troubles with Singaporean authorities began well before the allegations of espionage became public.

Singapore launched an investigation in February 2025 into suspected false declarations involving purchases of computer servers and their eventual destinations.

Police questioned Huang in June that year and retained her passport to ensure her availability during the investigation.

In February 2026, authorities determined that there was insufficient evidence to establish that she had committed offences related to the suspected false declarations.

However, Singapore's Ministry of Home Affairs said investigators believed Huang had knowingly supplied inaccurate information to minimize her involvement in Megaspeed.

She received a formal warning and was prohibited from returning to Singapore. Authorities returned her passport on February 26, and she left the country that day.

Taiwanese authorities have also revoked her entry permit.

Speaking in Australia on Tuesday, Singaporean Prime Minister Lawrence Wong reiterated that authorities had found no grounds to pursue prosecution against Huang, although investigations into Megaspeed were continuing.

Singapore has explicitly stated that its investigation of Huang did not concern espionage.

Bloomberg reported on November 12, citing anonymous sources, that Huang was in Beijing and that Chinese security officials were aware of her presence there. Her current whereabouts have not been independently confirmed.

Beijing has rejected the espionage allegations, while Huang herself has remained publicly silent in recent reporting.

Meanwhile, scrutiny of her business network continues to intensify.

On Wednesday, Reuters reported that companies connected to Huang's relatives and business associates had secured financing against AI servers and computing modules valued at $270 million in China.

The financial records did not establish whether the equipment contained chips subject to US export restrictions. Huang could not be reached for comment by Reuters.

The revelations followed Washington's decision on Monday to add Megaspeed and several related businesses to its trade blacklist.

While the latest intelligence assessment weakens the allegation that Huang was engaged in a Beijing-directed espionage operation, it does not settle the separate questions surrounding her commercial connections.

For now, Jensen Huang has reclaimed his position at one of the world's most influential technology companies. Alice Huang's professional future, however, remains uncertain.

In a post early Thursday, Zakura recommended users migrate any ZEC still in Sapling to Ironwood. These shielded pools allow users to hold and transfer ZEC without publicly revealing transaction amounts or sender and recipient addresses.

Roughly 400,000 ZEC, or approximately 2% of supply, remains in the pool, according to Zakura, worth roughly $291 million at current prices. Zakura said most wallets support both Sapling and Ironwood, and the impact should be minimal, with miners accounting for much of the activity left in Sapling.

"Less than 2.6% of all transactions in the last 30 days use Sapling, and of those, 66% are known miner flows, and it's highly likely most of the remainder are miners as well," the team said.

An earlier Zcash forum proposal in April had suggested waiting a year after a community decision to make Sapling withdrawal-only. At the time, the proposal put its balance at 600,000 ZEC, down from 1.1 million at the start of 2024. Zakura did not suggest a new deadline in its Thursday post.

Zakura pointed to a reported proof of the Riemann hypothesis, which concerns the distribution of prime numbers, and unsubstantiated rumors that AI labs had also made advances in integer factorization, the process of splitting large numbers into their prime factors. The difficulty of that task underpins RSA encryption, which is rarely used in cryptocurrencies, according to the team. Zakura said some math can be used for attacks on both RSA and pairing-based cryptography, so advances in one could help with the other, but the reported Riemann proof and the rumors do not show that either can be broken in practice.

"Practical pairing breaks are highly speculative," Zakura said, adding that transparent transactions and Ironwood do not rely on factoring or pairings.

Nevertheless, a hypothetical break in Sapling's pairing-based proof system would allow forged proofs, Zakura said, putting the funds in the pool at risk. The same cryptography does not secure users' private keys or their cryptographic records of shielded funds, so the team said developers could replace the proof system without replacing those records. However, Zcash would have to freeze Sapling before an attack compromises its state and users could then later recover their funds using a new ECDLP-based or hash-based SNARK, Zakura said.

Separately, the Ethereum Foundation doubled its protocol security team, The Block previously reported, arguing that AI is a "more urgent risk" than quantum computing and recommending Keccak-256 over four competing candidates for Ethereum's planned shift to hash-based cryptography. Zakura said it is also working on a proposal to add hash-based, post-quantum signatures for Zcash transparent transactions using SPHINCS+ with 192-bit security.

#4939. Want Headphones Built for Real Workouts? These 9 Survived Runs, Jumps, and Gym-Bag Chaos

Headphones that can handle as much as you can.

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

Listening to a hyped-up playlist can make all the difference in your workout. As a fitness writer and longtime distance runner, I’ve seen firsthand how the right headphones can make or break a workout. And I’ve worked my way through a range of workout headphones before I found the ones I don’t want to be without.

I used to constantly fiddle with headphones that didn’t fit right, which is a real motivational buzzkill, and once spent 10 minutes trying to hunt down an earbud that popped out mid-run. (I never recovered it.) I’ve also discovered that some headphones are better for certain types of workouts over others. Case in point: My go-to headphones for strength training at the noisy gym are different from what I reach for when it comes to HIIT and running.

No matter the style and fit you prefer, elements like sweat resistance, battery life, sound quality, and adjustability are crucial, too. And, while I love a good bargain, I’ve learned that you can’t just grab any random pair of cheap headphones or earbuds and expect them to do the job well. After multiple rounds of testing, these are the best wireless workout headphones to consider.

The Apple AirPods Pro have always been a reliable pair of headphones for me, and the latest third generation is even better. Whether I’m biking or struggling through heavy reps, it delivers a premium experience, including impressive sound and a comfortable fit. And the latest edition further proves their God-tier status: heart rate, step, and calorie tracking.

It has a sensor that deciphers your pulse through your ear canals, which then calculates calories burned based on heart rate. I like to keep tabs on my heart rate during high-intensity cardio, so it’s a great alternative to wearing a fitness tracker. Just make sure the fit is right to get an accurate reading (four silicone ear cup sizes are available).

It also has motion sensors that can track your steps. All data transfers to the Apple Health app, so you need to own an iPhone or iPad. Luckily, I recently converted (sorry, Android).

When I’m grinding hard at the gym, I want to hear nothing around me except my hype house music. The active noise cancellation drowns out any grunters, loud gym music, TVs, and general unnecessary background noise. I feel like it’s just me and my music, so that I can laser-focus on the task at hand.

But when I need to maintain awareness during outdoor runs, I turn on transparency mode to hear oncoming traffic and people nearby. I also like that it automatically lowers my music when it detects me talking to someone. It has an IP57 rating, meaning it’s sweat and dust-resistant, and can be submerged in a meter of water for up to 30 minutes in case of any accidental puddle drops (been there). As someone who sweats a lot, each bud repels moisture very well and doesn’t fall out of my ears when jumping or running. Plus, sweat never clogs my ears—something I experienced with regular AirPods. Battery life could be better for all-day wear, but it’s good for workouts (assuming you’re not working out all day). I hit the gym after work, and the power is always drained after an eight-hour day. On the flip side, it’s easy to juice up in 15 minutes with the charging case (it offers up to 30 hours of battery life per charge). To fully restore the battery, make sure to charge overnight. Read More: Best Fitness Trackers

The Bose QuietComfort Ultra Headphones are an absolute treasure. I own a lot of headphones, but the sound quality always keeps me coming back for more. The over-ear design completely covers my ears, providing A-grade noise cancellation at prime-time hours.

The sound is immersive with balanced, deep bass that doesn’t feel piercing—an issue with lower-quality headphones I tested. I blast my tunes at full volume when getting in the zone, and I never feel uncomfortable.

They look bulky, but looks can be deceiving. They never budge, even when speed walking at an incline or doing fast-paced plyometric drills. I’ve worn it during box jumps and ice skaters, and it stayed put.

Just note it’s not water resistant for intense cardio like spinning and running, where you’ll work up a sweat—although the plush padding rimming the headband and ear cups can easily be wiped clean.

Like the Apple AirPods Pro 3, I have to charge it daily in the included case, so make sure to keep the cable on hand for quick power-ups.

Read More: The Best Slim Fitness Trackers

If you really just can’t with the possibility of your earbuds falling out, but still want a compact option, Dr. Dre delivered just what you need: the Beats Powerbeats Pro 2. It has hooks that seamlessly glide over the ears, ensuring a proper fit that stays put. And compared to the previous iteration that launched six years ago, it’s now smaller and lighter, and shares many of the same features as the AirPods Pro 3 (Apple does own Beats, after all), including active noise cancellation, transparency mode, and heart rate monitoring through the Beats app.

I’ve put it to the test during long runs, sprints, low-impact biking, and strength training. The verdict? It performs as sleekly as it looks. The sound is crisp and rich, while the bass is heavy without being overbearing.The sweat resistance is a notch below AirPods with an IPX4 rating, meaning it can withstand light rain but can’t be submerged. I’ve gotten caught in the rain one too many times while wearing these—yet, the sound quality is still the same as it was straight out of the box. And battery life is actually slightly better than AirPods, offering up to 45 hours with the charging case.However, this pair feels more uncomfortable than the Apple AirPods Pro 3. The material feels a little too hard for my liking. If you plan on walking or running for hours, the best overall is the way to go.

The last thing you want is uncomfortable headphones when in the midst of PRing your next barbell squat. Working out is tough enough, so having a pair that’s übersoft will take away some of the pain. Meet the Sony WH-1000XM6—a splurge that’s worth the investment.

Thick foam on the ear cups feels like lying on a pillow, while it also seals sound better for superior noise cancellation. The wide headband is plush and fits securely onto the head without being too tight. MH senior gear and commerce editor Ryan Brower throws it in his gym bag whenever he has strength training on deck. He also appreciates the adjustable smooth slider for a custom fit, calling it a fluid mechanism.

The headphones use 12 microphones to isolate and cancel out sound to deliver an immersive listening experience. Vocals and instruments sound balanced and rich, with Brower calling the sound quality superb. Battery life can run for up to 30 hours, while just three minutes of charging can provide three hours—perfect if you’re in a rush to hit the gym.

Brower’s only gripes are the lack of sweat resistance for high-intensity activities, like running or spinning, and that it feels a little bulky. So, he reserves it for less strenuous pursuits.

If you’re into an over-ear design in headphones, you know they can get hot and sweaty fast. But the Skullcandy Crusher 540 headphones feel surprisingly breathable on—for an over-ear headphone. The ear cups are made from a lightweight material that feels breezy against your ears, minimizing extra sweating while you work out.

These headphones also have an impressive battery life of 40 hours, which is only second on our list to the Powerbeats Pro 2. Skullcandy clearly designed these headphones for convenience, with plenty of buttons within easy reach. As a result, you can quickly turn the volume up or down without missing a beat. If active noise cancellation is a must for you, scroll up—while the sound quality on these headphones is excellent, they won’t help you fully tune out the world.

The Skullcandy Crusher 540 headphones don’t have an official IPX rating, but they have a special sweat- and water-resistant nano-coating to protect your gear. (The ear cup pads are also removable for easy cleaning.) A big draw of these headphones is the strong bass, which comes in handy during tough workouts. As someone who loses nearly everything, I appreciate the built-in Tile technology to help you find your headphones with the Tile app if you misplace them.

I first tested the Bose Open Ultra Earbuds last fall, and they’ve been my favorite pair for distance running ever since. These earbuds aren’t going anywhere thanks to a design that’s similar to a clip-on earring. Just gently hook these on your ears and move on. The style is perfect for people like me who have been burned in the past by an earbud falling out and vanishing forever.

As an early morning runner who regularly crosses streets, I appreciate the open-ear audio these earbuds deliver. I can hear my music perfectly, but still can detect things like chirping birds to give me a solid awareness of my surroundings. You can adjust the volume, skip songs, and flip between immersive and stereo sound with a tap on your earbuds, making it easy to switch things up mid-run.

A heads up: If you’ve never used an earbud style like this in the past, you may need to give your ears a little time to build up to wearing them. My ears were a little sore when I first started wearing the Open Ultra Earbuds, but I don’t even feel them when they’re on now. These earbuds are also IPX4 rated for water resistance, so they do just fine with light splashes or rain—just make sure you don't wear these to swim laps.

The earbuds have a seven-hour battery life, which is lower than several others on this list. But I’ve never had an issue with them dying on me. I just pop them in their charging case when they’re not in use.

Some people are going to struggle to get earbuds to fit, no matter what they do. If you have smaller ears and you’re over flipping through different ear tips in hopes something will fit, the Beats Powerbeats Fit are a solid choice. These earbuds actually fit inside your ears like a hearing aid with the help of flexible wingtips that really lock them in there.

These earbuds are small, but they deliver the top-tier sound quality you’ve come to expect from Beats. That includes the options to flip between active noise cancellation and transparency modes, so you can use these to tune out loud gym-goers or to be aware of your surroundings during outdoor workouts.

These earbuds pair seamlessly with Apple and Android phones, making them an equal opportunity headphone. They also have an IPX4 rating for sweat and splash resistance, so you can wear them in the rain, but not to swim laps. While the Powerbeats Fit comes with four different tips, your ears will still need a little time to get used to these before wearing them on, say, a 10-miler.

The earbuds do kind of jam in there, and it can take some time to get used to the feel of the wingtips. But if you’re looking for a discreet pair of headphones that aren’t going anywhere, you can stop your search here.

If you want secure earbuds that aren’t an investment, the Anker Soundcore Sport X20 fits the bill. It costs a third of the Beats Powerbeats Pro 2 and shares the same ear-hook design that doesn’t budge when pushing your limits during high-impact workouts. The sound is shockingly premium given the $80 price tag. If I were doing a blind test, I’d think it costs at least $200.

The strong noise cancellation blocks out every peep imaginable at the gym. From loud gym music to weights slamming, I can’t hear a thing except my jams. But when I don’t want to be super locked in, I switch to “normal” mode so I can listen to background noise. This mode is handy when running or walking at night. And when things get too wet during intense grinding sessions, the IP67 sweat-resistance saves me. Although I haven’t tested it while swimming, it can withstand water submersion beyond one meter for about 30 minutes.

The silicone ear hooks are soft, flexible, and extremely comfortable. I find myself reaching for it outside of the gym and often forget it’s even on my ears, which I’m not mad about—it makes a great cool-girl accessory. The only downside of wearing it for too long is that the battery will drain after about eight hours. Luckily, the charging case has two days' worth of battery life—so no excuses to skip a workout.

The Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 are my go-to for long-distance running because of the wrap-around and open-ear design that stays in place. It’s no surprise it’s a TikTok-viral favorite among runners and our editors.

The sweat-resistance rating is one notch below our best overall, with an IP55 score, meaning it can withstand intense rain during rough outdoor conditions. Moisture from sweat is never an issue since the design hangs over the ear and doesn’t go in the canal. It even alerts me with a vibrating beep if moisture is present in the port while charging.

If blocking out noise is your priority, you should consider other options, as this pair doesn’t offer noise cancellation. I don’t love that I can’t be fully engaged in my music, but that’s the trade-off for running safely. Unlike other headphones I tested in this guide, the sound emits outside of the eardrum using bone conduction technology, which is when noise is transmitted through vibrations in the skull to reach the ear. I hear every sound, from people talking to traffic, so I give it a perfect score for maintaining awareness. I deem it an essential pair if you train early in the mornings or at night. Just note it’s not going to be the same listening experience as the Apple AirPods Pro 3, for example.

The battery life is nowhere near the capacity of the Apple AirPods Pro 3, with only about 12 hours of playtime, so I find I have to charge it weekly for an hour. The flip side is that it only takes 10 minutes to get two hours of battery life if I quickly need it before a run.

Full disclosure: They come in two sizes, but tend to run large, which is why I went with the mini size. I ordered the standard size first and had to return them (small head probs).

If you plan on running, spinning, or doing other high-intensity training, it’s best to have headphones that can withstand sweat. They should have an IP rating, which is a protection score for how well electronics can resist water. “IPX4 or higher is perfect for working out,” says Joe Smith, an audio specialist at Music Critic. All options on this list have at least an IPX4 rating.

But our best budget option, the Anker Soundcore Sport X20, has an even better score of IP67, meaning it can handle being submerged in just over one meter of water for 30 minutes. If headphones aren’t made to withstand sweat, it’s best to reserve those for lower-intensity workouts.

Having your headphones die during a half-marathon is not the vibe (been there). Using a pair with good battery life is crucial to ensuring the tunes are always going strong during a long workout. With select pairs, it can be dependent on whether or not select features are in use.

For example, the total playtime for the new Apple AirPods Pro 3 from a single charge (with case) is up to 10 hours with active noise cancellation turned off, but only up to eight hours with it turned on. Carl Prouty, a tech expert at Abt, recommends snagging a model that charges fast in case you forget to plug them in the night before.

Noise cancellation is a function that utilizes a microphone hidden inside the earbud or earcup to analyze frequencies that emit opposite sound waves, thus helping to reduce background noise. Blocking out surrounding noise is great for staying focused and immersed, but it’s not the safest feature in desolate areas like quiet trails, busy streets, or at night.

I prefer an open-ear style to maintain awareness during outdoor runs. If you’re not a fan of that design, other options on this list allow you to turn noise cancellation on and off. “If you still want to be able to hear what's going on around you while also listening to music, look for a model with a good ambient and pass-through mode,” says Prouty.

You have a lot to choose from in a workout headphone, and each has its pros and cons. Earbuds rest inside your ears to deliver sound without bulk. These tend to fit comfortably, but may pop out if you don’t get the fit right. Ear hook earbuds add an extra layer—a hook that goes over your ears—to help combat this issue. There are also open-style headphones that hook over your ears and around the back of your head to keep them in place.

A newer category of these is open earbuds that clip over your ear like a clip-on earring, while nestling into your ear like an earbud. Finally, over-ear headphones have soft cups that fit over your ear for a classic look. While these usually do a good job staying in place, they may feel hotter during intense workouts than other designs.

As a distance runner, I rely on good music to keep me hyped up and entertained on long runs. I’ve tested dozens of pairs of wireless headphones for working out over the past decade and learned what features make pairs stand out. Only workout headphones with good sweat resistance, battery life, noise cancellation, and sound transparency made the final cut.

Because everyone has different needs in a workout headphone, I also leaned on experiences from Women’s Health editors, along with Men’s Health senior gear and reviews editor Ryan Brower. Each pair was used in different environments during cardio and strength training sessions to see how they performed when put to the test during workouts. Those included 5- to 10-mile runs, indoor cycling workouts, HIIT sessions, and more general lifting at the gym.

#4937. JPMorgan says bitcoin ‘capitulation’ signaled by Strategy’s record-low NAV multiple

Looking for institutional-grade crypto trading? Discover LMAX Digital, the regulated exchange from LMAX Group

JPMorgan said Strategy's NAV multiple has fallen to around 0.88x, below the previous low seen in late June.

JPMorgan analysts said the recent drop in Strategy's valuation relative to its bitcoin holdings to a record low signals "capitulation" in the bitcoin Bitcoin (BTC) market.

The ratio has fallen to around 0.88x, below the previous low seen in late June, JPMorgan analysts led by Nikolaos Panigirtzoglou wrote in a Wednesday report. The analysts' charts compare Strategy's enterprise value with the dollar value of its bitcoin holdings, though the report does not specify the exact formula used.

Strategy has its own way of calculating the ratio, which it calls mNAV. The company divides its common share price by the dollar value of its net bitcoin holdings per share, taking into account its debt, preferred claims, and U.S. dollar assets, according to its website.

Strategy's dashboard showed an mNAV of 0.88x at 10:39 a.m. ET on Nov. 25, which later rose to 0.94x. Both figures are based on Strategy's own calculation.

"The premium to NAV collapses to a new record low of 0.88 for MicroStrategy’s stock, signaling capitulation in bitcoin," the analysts wrote.

Bitcoin has fallen back to around $60,000 after recovering briefly from last week's lows.

BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT), the largest spot bitcoin exchange-traded fund by market capitalization, continued to see outflows even during the brief price recovery, the analysts said. "Indeed, the speed of the outflows has, if anything, been more intense than the outflows from early May to late June this year," they added.

Last week, the analysts said retail investors likely drove much of the recent crypto ETF outflows and may have sold to buy stock ETFs. They also said bitcoin's price drop had widened the gap between its market price and their estimated production cost of around $86,000, likely adding pressure on higher-cost miners to sell bitcoin from their reserves.

#4936. China's Google Just Released Its Fast New AI Model for Free

China's Google Just Released Its Fast New AI Model for Free

Baidu, China's equivalent of Google, released its ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview AI model this week, giving developers worldwide free access to a high-speed reasoning model designed to handle complex coding and autonomous tasks at relatively low computational costs.

The release comes nearly two weeks after Baidu introduced the model through its cloud computing platform. Developers can now download it, modify it and build commercial products around it under the permissive Apache 2.0 license, without paying Baidu for every interaction.

Baidu has been pursuing computational efficiency for some time. In May, the company released ERNIE 5.1, claiming its pre-training cost was just 6% of that of comparable AI models.

You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Anthropic, Nvidia, Google and more with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.

ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview uses a mixture-of-experts architecture, which divides the neural network into specialized subnetworks. The model has 280 billion parameters—the numerical values that encode what an AI learned during training—but uses only 14 billion to process each token.

Baidu also compressed most of the model's weights to four-bit precision to reduce memory consumption and incorporated a technique called speculative decoding, which drafts several tokens in parallel for the main model to verify. Its context window exceeds one million tokens, allowing it to process hundreds of thousands of words within a single session.

In one demonstration, Baidu tasked the model with developing a third-person martial arts video game using Unreal Engine 5.8. The model spent 11 hours writing code, integrating existing graphical assets and iteratively fixing bugs, despite being unable to process images natively.

On Terminal-Bench 4.0, which measures an AI agent's ability to complete computer tasks through a command-line interface, ERNIE achieved 46.5%. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash scored 42.3%, GLM-5.3-Flash achieved 35.8%, and OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol scored 56.1%.

The Chinese model also outperformed both GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5 on AutomationBench, which evaluates business workflows across different applications. ERNIE scored 61.9%, compared with 49.3% for GPT and 58% for Claude, according to Baidu's evaluations.

These are manufacturer-reported results, however, and the evaluations use different software environments for some competing models.

Baidu's international API pricing is $0.28 per million input tokens and $1.13 per million output tokens. The model is also available through a free tier on OpenRouter.

The decision to release the model puts Baidu alongside Chinese competitors like Alibaba and DeepSeek, which have made increasingly capable AI models available for businesses to run on their own infrastructure.

For Baidu, giving away a model could help attract developers to an ecosystem where the company makes money selling computing resources. Its AI cloud infrastructure revenue grew 94% year over year in the third quarter, helping offset weakness in its advertising business.

The model is technically open-weight rather than fully open-source AI, since the release does not provide everything necessary to reproduce its training. Running it independently also requires substantial hardware: Even its most compressed official version contains approximately 166 GB of model files.

Baidu says the model is still undergoing training and has yet to announce a date for the final release of ERNIE 5.5 Flash.

#4934. The Best Matching Sweat Sets, Tested by Style and Fitness Editors

Just in time for Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals.

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

Back in the day, a sweatsuit was all about comfort. It wasn’t so much a fashion staple, but the kind of thing to throw on and lounge in. With Y2K style back in vogue, matching sweatsuits are more commonplace than ever—just with a little less sparkle than the ones previously sported by icons like Paris Hilton and J.Lo in the early 2000s. And, with the rise of athleisure, these simple sweats have gotten the luxury treatment: they’re softer, more flattering, and pricier than ever.

Whether you’re the kind of person who considers it a cozy wardrobe essential, or you’re just looking to treat yourself to something comfortable to wear around the house, there have never been more choices when it comes to the best matching sweatsuits. Since we’re heading into winter (and Black Friday is just around the corner!), Women’s Health editors tested the most popular styles.

Here are our thoughts on the matching sets after months of lounging in them, working from home in them, and even wearing them to work.

Oner Active’s workout clothes have had our hearts at WH for a while. That’s why we were excited to put their loungewear to the test. Associate Health and Fitness editor Addison Aloian wore this set while traveling, chilling at home, and even working behind the scenes on a photoshoot.

“I absolutely love this set from Oner,” she says. She loves it for its comfort, warmth, and versatility (Aloian says she knows she could wear it outside in the chilly NYC winter, layer it under her ski clothes, or pop it on over leggings for her warm-up at the gym). “But the standout feature is the color,” Aloian says. “So many sweat sets are gray or black, but the turquoise is stunning and makes it a standout in my closet when I want a monochromatic moment.” She opted for the “oil blue” color, but Oner also has options like alpine green and toasted red, plus your neutral staples.

It’s also one of the more affordable options we tested—and on sale for half off this Black Friday. But that doesn’t mean it skimps on quality: The material feels super plush since it’s made from 67% cotton and 33% polyester, for a super plush feel that doesn’t pill or shed after one wash.

The set’s one flaw? The bottoms are a little long. At 5 '1, Aloian says she’d love a “short” option as well. Oner does offer a “long” length, though, for the taller girlies.

Old Navy Bounce Fleece Half-Zip Pullover Sweatshirt

Old Navy High-Waisted Bounce Fleece Jogger Sweatpants

In a world of expensive sweat sets, Old Navy’s Bounce Fleece line provides a budget-friendly—and stylish—option. “You’d never know these are super affordable,” says Fitness editor Cori Ritchey. They hold their own with the rest of the pricier sets from their fit to their feel.

The highlight for Ritchey is the material, a mix of polyester, rayon, and spandex. “It moves with you, and the fabric feels like it breathes compared to other sweatsuits that feel too heavy and hot.” One small caveat: Be sure to follow the wash instructions and keep your cycle on cold and gentle, tumble dry low, and keep the garments inside out. Ritchey says she noticed a bit of pilling after the first wash, but says that after following the wash instructions during the next few washes, the set stayed in great shape.

The half-zip and jogger combo makes for a put-together look and is cozy enough for traveling, running errands, or lounging around the house, Ritchey says. The set comes in plenty of neutral colors, plus some fun ones like orchid. It’s also the first on our list that doesn’t have a prominent logo, for anyone who wants a clean-looking set with no branding. Another point for Old Navy: It’s the most size-inclusive on the list. Sizing goes from XS to 4XL, with regular, tall, and petite options.

Alo is another longtime favorite at WH. The brand is known for its cozy, stylish (and premium-priced) loungewear. The fit is what we love most. The set, which comes in over a dozen colors, has an oversized feel, yet still manages to look intentional, says Deputy Features editor Carina Hsieh. “Unlike other sweatsuits, this one doesn’t look or feel unflattering or sloppy,” she says. She especially likes how it falls on her shoulders.

It’s also the “perfect transition-weather sweatsuit.” The French terry material is made up of 65% cotton and 35% polyester, for a “really soft, thick, and high-quality” feel. The fabric doesn’t feel ultra-heavy, though, so it’s a great pick for fall and spring when you might overheat in thicker sets. Another perk? The pants have pockets.

An onchain trade requires both the tokenized asset itself and an onchain payment that clears it. Most of this year's progress has been focused on the asset. Last week bank money started to move onchain too.

Last Tuesday, Fed Governor Christopher Waller said that central bank money needs to stay the foundation of tokenized markets, with stables and tokenized deposits built on top.

Singapore has made progress toward that end. MAS sold S$100M (about US$77M) of 4-week bills issued natively on its own ledger, paid in wholesale central bank digital currency. Demand was significant, with bids coming in at more than two times the amount offered, with MAS planning more issuance and wider use as collateral in 2027.

Commercial banks are seeing the value in tokenized deposits too. Ant International launched a pilot program with DBS and Franklin Templeton for a protocol that settles tokenized deposits directly against tokenized money market funds.

The assets on the other side are already onchain. Tokenized Treasury and money market funds hold $14.1B, up 55% this year, though down from a peak of about $16B in July. The drop since July stems mostly from BlackRock's BUIDL and Circle's USYC, with the rest of the market increasing to a record $10.5B. As bank and central bank money scale onchain, institutions will be able to buy tokenized assets 24/7 with regulated deposits instead of private stablecoins.

Anthropic listed on Nasdaq on Nov 19, and tokenized versions from several issuers were trading onchain the same day. Across the 4 tracked by RWA.xyz, holders doubled from 2,161 on Nov 19 to 4,335 by Nov 22. xStocks' ANTx holds $25M of the $30M in combined market value.

With one stock split across many tokens, we expect liquidity to concentrate around tokens that redeem into real shares. Alpaca provides exactly that service and has processed $10B in minting and redemption.

Tokenized sterling government debt has roughly quadrupled since the end of September, from about $20M to $83M, according to RWA.xyz. That makes sterling the third-largest currency in tokenized government debt outside the US dollar. Most of the increase came from Aviva Investors, which launched a fund on the XRP Ledger in October and seeded it with £50M of its own capital.

The UK is also planning to issue the first digital gilt on HSBC's Orion platform by Q1 2027. That will make the UK the first G7 nation to issue tokenized sovereign debt and will create a model for other governments.

New York Wins $1.37B Judgment Against NovaTech Founders Who Fled the US

A New York court has ordered the founders of collapsed crypto trading platform NovaTech to pay $1.37 billion for running a Ponzi scheme that targeted Haitian immigrant communities, Attorney General Letitia James said on Wednesday.

Cynthia and Eddy Petion, along with NovaTech and related companies, are jointly liable for $1.13 billion in disgorgement plus $232.5 million in interest, for a total of $1,367,023,585, according to court documents in the case, which is before Justice Anar Rathod Patel in the Commercial Division of New York's Supreme Court.

We won a historic $1.3 billion judgment against the founders of crypto company NovaTech for defrauding hundreds of thousands of people, including Haitian immigrants in New York.

We'll always fight to bring fraudsters who take advantage of New Yorkers to justice.

— NY AG James (@NewYorkStateAG) November 25, 2026

Cynthia Petion and AWS Mining, a crypto mining company the couple promoted before founding NovaTech, were also ordered to pay a further $6.2 million combined for the AWS Mining scheme.

"NovaTech cruelly targeted immigrant families through faith and community groups with the promise of a better life while robbing them of their life savings," James said in a statement.

The judgment follows a default ruling in August 2025, after the Petions fled the country and failed to respond to the lawsuit. That ruling also banned them from the securities, commodities and crypto industries, and the court then decided how much they owed.

In October, James' office asked the court to set the damages at about $1.37 billion. The Petions failed to comply with a court order to provide a full accounting of payments to and from investors, according to the court documents.

Collecting the money may prove difficult. The couple was allegedly living in Panama when James first sued in June 2024, Reuters reported at the time.

James' office sued NovaTech and AWS Mining in June 2024, alleging that they targeted immigrant communities, particularly Haitian New Yorkers, through prayer groups, social media and WhatsApp chats, with false promises of high returns, while running illegal pyramid schemes. The schemes defrauded hundreds of thousands of investors worldwide, including about 11,000 New Yorkers, according to the attorney general.

The Securities and Exchange Commission charged the Petions and NovaTech promoters in August 2024, alleging the firm raised more than $650 million from over 200,000 investors.

Four promoters in the New York case, Martin Zizi, Frantz Ciceron, Ricardo Roy Sr. and James Corbett, have agreed to pay nearly $6 million and have been permanently banned from the securities, commodities and crypto industries.

#4930. The 5 Best Laser Hair Growth Devices for Men in 2026, According to Doctors

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

You don’t need to fly overseas to regrow hair.

THERE COMES A time in every man’s life—sans the few genetically gifted—when he must face hair loss. It hits sooner than many expect, as the American Hair Loss Association notes that 85 percent of men will face hair loss by age 50. There are then two options: lean into it and join the Stanley Tucci Gang, or invest in equipment to regrow hair. For the latter, the best tools to reverse balding at home are laser hair growth devices.

The majority of men lose their hair due to male pattern baldness (also known as androgenetic alopecia), a condition caused by genetic predisposition and hormonal influences, wherein testosterone is declining and dihydrotestosterone (aka DHT) is surging. This process is characterized by the classic receding hairline look, along with thinning around the crown.

Laser hair growth devices are best at treating this cause of hair loss, explains dermatologist and founder of Remedy, Dr. Muneeb Shah, MD. Other common factors like stress, illness, medications, nutritional deficiencies, and autoimmune diseases will be less responsive to laser therapies, as hair follicles are often damaged or inactive from these issues and less willing to be rebooted from light treatment.

Laser hair growth devices work by using low-level laser therapy, or LLLT, to stimulate weakened or dormant hair follicles, says hair restoration physician and creator of the Bauman Turbo LaserCap, Dr. Alan Bauman, MD. The process is known as photobiomodulation, and it involves exposing tissues to light in the red and near-infrared spectrum, which can improve cell metabolism and blood flow, reduce inflammation, and stimulate hair follicles to re-enter and maintain the growth phase.

Generally, LLLT does not include LED; instead, it uses laser diodes. However, some devices will combine both for added effectiveness or to reduce the intensity of laser diodes. “In simpler terms, laser therapy supercharges the environment for healthy hair growth by restoring energy to sluggish follicles and optimizing scalp conditions,” Dr. Bauman says.

Laser hair growth devices are rarely cheap (you won’t find an effective one below $400), so you want to make sure you’re getting the right option for you before making the investment. After chatting with the pros, these are the five laser hair growth devices worth considering.

The biggest dilemma when buying a laser hair growth device is choosing between LED and laser diodes, but with the iRestore Laser Therapy Hair Growth System, you don’t have to. This device uses a hybrid of laser diodes and LEDs to get the best of both worlds, pairing the gentle nature of LEDs with the power of laser diodes. Dr. Shah backs it, noting that iRestore is reputable and the device is FDA-cleared.

The brand even offers a six-month money-back guarantee if no results are seen. However, I’d imagine the brand doesn’t receive many sendbacks, as this device gives full coverage with serious results. That being said, Dr. Bauman warns that the combo of LED and laser diodes may dilute benefits for some due to mixed light sources. But hard to argue with a six-month guarantee.

Read More: iRestore Laser Face Mask Pro Review

Dr. Shah also recommends this offering from Current Body. This futuristic helmet offers a spectrum of red light LED from 620 to 660 nanometers. The flexible intensity allows for a customized experience, which is ideal for those new to these tools or with sensitive skin to ease into LED treatment and see what your ideal nanometer level is.

While results will be stronger closer to 650 or 660 nanometers, this range is powerful enough to reduce inflammation, decrease DHT levels (to maintain follicle strength), and improve blood flow on the scalp (to provide hair follicles with more oxygen and nutrients needed for growth).

Sure, it may look like a VR set from a scrapped Black Mirror episode, but it’s quite comfortable, and deceptively adjustable for a quality fit. Use for 10 minutes daily, and results can be seen quickly in as little as 16 weeks. The only reasons this helmet missed out on the top spot is that it relies solely on LED, and is roughly $300 more expensive than iRestore’s helmet.

Not everybody has the budget (or desire) to drop several thousand on a hair growth device. Maybe you’re on the fence about these tools, or the prospect of regrowing your hair in general. For these folks, Hairmax will be your best option, as it’s the least expensive tool on the market that’s still effective.

Featuring 12 medical-grade laser diodes in a comb-style tool, you gently brush this device through your hair and across your dome to stimulate hair growth. The sessions are listed at eight minutes; however, it often takes longer for the best results, given the manual nature of the device and the smaller surface it covers at once. Still, you won’t find a cheaper FDA-approved model.

Read More: Is Your Hair Loss From Thinning or Breaking

At first glance, the Hairmax LaserBand 82 looks like a nuisance to use. Rather than a cap design like HigherDose and Capillus, helmet like iRestore and Current Body, or Hairmax’s comb, the LaserBand resembles a mini MRI machine. But unlike those devices, this tool only needs to be used for a couple of minutes to see results, three times a week.

The brand boasts that sessions need only be 90 seconds, but Dr. Bauman warns it’ll take a bit longer for full coverage—like two or three minutes. Still, that’s by far the quickest treatment on this list. Plus, Dr. Bauman says it features a quality diode count (246 lasers), even if you may need to reposition after 90 seconds for full coverage.

Read More: Best Hair Thickening Shampoos for Men

Men’s Health writer Bob Gearing wore the HigherDose Red Light Therapy Hat every day for the past year, and swears by the results. He notes that this nifty cap is both more effective than Rogaine and less invasive, leaving no irritation or redness. It’s super easy to use, pop it on like any hat, and wear for 10 minutes a day while the 650 nanometer LED red light penetrates the scalp to promote a healthier environment for hair growth.

The brand lists 16 months as the target, but the best results will appear after six months. Unlike the Capillus cap, whose red light peaks through the sides during use, this is the only hair growth device you could get away with wearing in public without anyone noticing. It simply looks like a black hat, nothing more. This makes it both easy to use and even easier to incorporate into your daily routine.

As Dr. Bauman puts it, not all laser hair growth devices are created equal. The first thing to consider is what light is being used in your device to stimulate growth. The two primary options are LEDs (Light Emitting Diodes) and laser diodes. He recommends zeroing in on laser diodes as they’re more powerful and penetrate deeper into the scalp, targeting the hair follicle root more effectively.

From a strict regrowth perspective, laser diodes will be more effective; however, these also present more potential side effects given their strength, such as hyperpigmentation, burns, redness, and swelling. LEDs present fewer side effects, so they’re better for sensitive scalps, but they won’t penetrate the scalp and hair follicles as deeply. This means LED is best suited for early shedding and will struggle to help more severe hair loss.

For both LED and laser diode options, the therapeutic wavelength is crucial. Dr. Shah recommends wavelengths between 630 and 680 nanometers to successfully penetrate the scalp and stimulate hair follicle growth. If you have sensitive skin or are new to these tools, take it slow and work your way to the top level to limit irritation.

Dr. Bauman says that the 650-nanometer range is key, as it is the optimal wavelength absorbed by mitochondria for energy production to support hair follicle function. This process boosts cellular energy, as hair follicles are highly active structures that need a lot of energy to support the hair growth cycle. The end result is reduced inflammation, improved blood flow, and extended growth.

To be clear, no laser hair growth device is going to give you Thor-level flow overnight—these tools take time. Dr. Shah says that men will need at least six months of consistent use before seeing results after regular use. But not every device’s session will be the same. Some, you’ll need to wear or place near the dome for five minutes, while others for half an hour. Consider the comfort of your device, along with your schedule, before investing.

Most importantly, however, Dr. Shah says consistency is crucial because missing sessions, no matter how long they are, can reduce the device’s effectiveness. If executed properly, early results will appear around six months, such as reduced shedding or slight thickening, before fuller regrowth occurs near the one-year mark, according to Dr. Shah.

Whenever you’re dealing with new technology, rely on reputable organizations to first approve it for use. Both Dr. Shah and Dr. Bauman advise only looking to laser hair growth devices that have been accepted by the FDA for the safest, most effective experience. However, there are different levels of FDA acceptance. FDA-listed or FDA-registered simply means that the manufacturer has informed the FDA, but doesn’t imply approval or authorization.

FDA clearance, on the other hand, means the device is substantially equivalent to a product already on the market.

FDA approved is the ideal, as this means the device has successfully been through extensive testing and clinical trials to demonstrate safety and effectiveness. But to date, there have been no LED or laser diode devices for hair growth that are FDA-approved, so look for FDA-cleared options.

As someone whose hairline is still going strong after 33 years (and a ton of preventive hair thinning products), I leaned heavily on the counsel of hair loss professionals for these selections. I conferred with dermatologist Dr. Shah and hair restoration physician Dr. Bauman on what to look for in an effective laser hair growth device and which they recommend.

I also consulted with fellow Men’s Health writers and editors who have battled hair loss on their experience, based on ease of use, effectiveness, and long-term results. Following this research and testing, we nailed down these tools as the five best laser hair growth devices for men in 2026.

A racerback style bra, the style in which the straps meet at the back to create an X or Y shape, happens to be a sort of Goldilocks bra option that suits most sizes because they’re super customizable. As a style writer who’s tested more bras than I can count (at different weights and sizes over the years), I’ve found that racerback sports bras tend to work especially well for smaller and larger busts alike. That’s part of why racerback bras have such a loyal following: they’re supportive, comfortable, less likely to slip around, and easy to style under a variety of workout tops.

This is especially true for bras with added features like underwire, molded cups, or a wider band, says Dani Read, a senior designer for luxury lingerie brand Cosabella. Adjustable straps (as opposed to fixed backs) can also help you get the right fit in a racerback, she adds. Racerback bras are a go-to style for Women’s Health’s style and fitness team, and for this guide, we’ve selected some of our favorites that we reach for again and again.

#4925. UK Regulator Cites Binance Hack as It Plans Tougher DeFi Rules Than US and EU: Report

UK Regulator Cites Binance Hack as It Plans Tougher DeFi Rules Than US and EU: Report

Britain's Financial Conduct Authority plans to require decentralized finance platforms to be authorized under its incoming crypto rules, taking a harder line than regulators in the U.S. or EU, the Financial Times reported on Thursday.

FCA officials told the newspaper they were deliberately strict on DeFi because they saw a high risk of fraud, scams and money laundering, and because users had little ability to recover stolen funds or seek compensation.

The regulator pointed to the record $6.4 billion hack of Binance in October. While Binance is a centralized exchange, the hackers moved large sums through decentralized exchanges, which do not freeze stolen funds, swapping them into other tokens to make them harder to trace.

"The speed and scale at which stolen funds move through DeFi platforms can frustrate attempts to freeze and block" transfers, Jane Moore, the FCA's head of department for payments and digital assets, told the FT.

You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short ETH with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.

The FCA's position means UK-regulated crypto trading platforms will not be allowed to execute retail trades on DeFi platforms. Moore said that divide between the regulated and unregulated sectors was deliberate, given the lack of consumer protections in DeFi.

The regulator also plans to require all UK retail orders for equities, tokenized or not, to be executed on a regulated platform, cutting off access to offshore DeFi venues for tokenized stocks. The same risk should be treated the same way, Jamie Bell, the FCA's head of capital markets, told the newspaper. The FCA and the Bank of England have set out a shared vision for tokenization within the regulated system.

After consulting on its wider crypto rules earlier this year, the FCA in October published draft guidance on how its rules apply to firms providing services that use or interact with DeFi. The consultation closed on November 18, and the regulator expects to publish final guidance in January 2027, ahead of its crypto regime taking effect on October 25, 2027.

Crypto firms argue the approach will leave UK investors without access to products such as tokenized equities and decentralized lending.

Linda Jeng, chief legal and policy officer at Aave Labs, which builds products for decentralized lending protocol Aave, called the FCA's position "highly problematic" and has written to the regulator asking it to clarify which DeFi service providers its rules would cover, according to the FT.

Coinbase's head of policy in Europe, Katie Harries, said that where the U.S. and EU are building rules for regulated DeFi access, the UK is "creating a prohibition." In September, the EU's European Securities and Markets Authority proposed a new regulated service under the bloc's MiCA rules for crypto firms that give customers access to DeFi protocols.

UK trade group CryptoUK has also urged the FCA not to treat DeFi developers as regulated by default, warning in its consultation response that parts of the proposed guidance go further than the law.

Orest Gavryliak, chief legal officer at DeFi aggregator 1inch, argued that financial crime is a challenge across all of finance, and that DeFi's transparency is a strength. "Every transaction is recorded on a public ledger, so illicit flows can be traced in a way that closed systems do not allow," he said.

A one-size-fits-all approach "would limit access to innovation without meaningfully reducing risk," Gavryliak said, adding that regulators could draw on industry tools such as wallet screening to design proportionate, risk-based rules.

Harry Halpin, CEO of decentralized VPN provider Nym, told Decrypt that a truly decentralized DeFi platform would be very hard to regulate, since there should be no central party to oversee. "If the government attempts then to block or censor access to these platforms, and so slowly built a Great Firewall of Britain, people will simply use a VPN," he said.

#4921. China, Japan, South Korea and ASEAN to form working group on digital payments, crypto regulation

Looking for institutional-grade crypto trading? Discover LMAX Digital, the regulated exchange from LMAX Group

The decision comes after the group met in May in Uzbekistan and identified cross-border digital payments as a new area of cooperation.

China, Japan, South Korea, and ASEAN member countries have agreed to set up a dedicated working group on cross-border digital payments and digital asset regulation.

According to a statement released Thursday, finance and central bank deputies gathered in Kyoto, Japan, this week to review progress in implementing the guidance set earlier by the ASEAN+3 finance ministers and central bank governors.

One major focus of the meeting was technological innovation, with discussions centering around cross-border payments and regulatory approaches to crypto assets. The deputies agreed to form the AMRO Cross-Border Digital Payments Program and a dedicated working group to support further policy talks.

The Kyoto decision is a result of a May meeting in Uzbekistan that identified cross-border digital payments as a new area of cooperation.

At that meeting, the group instructed deputies to establish modalities by the end of 2026 to deepen policy discussions on retail and wholesale payment connectivity, as well as regulatory approaches to stablecoins.

"Building on local currency‑based payment systems, technological innovation in cross‑border payments, such as tokenization, should be pursued in consistency with ongoing global discussions on policy […]," the group said in a May statement.

According to AMRO’s job post published last week seeking a consultant on cross-border retail payments, the initiative could cover research into a range of use cases, including person-to-person and person-to-merchant payments, tourism, e-commerce, and remittances.

Finance ministers and central bank governors are expected to further discuss the matter at the next meeting in Nagoya, Japan, in May 2027.

ASEAN+3 is an international cooperation framework that brings together 11 ASEAN member states and China, Japan, and South Korea. The 14 economies regularly convene to discuss political-security, economic, and socio-cultural matters.

The push for closer regional cooperation comes as Asian economies step up efforts to explore and test stablecoin and tokenization initiatives. Last month, the central banks of Malaysia and Thailand joined Singapore's BLOOM initiative to work on cross-border payments involving stablecoins and tokenized deposits.

Japan's top financial regulators are also studying tokenization of Japanese government bonds and a blockchain-based settlement system for stocks and Japanese government bonds. South Korea, meanwhile, is preparing tokenized securities from 2027 and local won stablecoins under its draft Digital Asset Basic Act.

Earlier this month, the central banks of the UK, Singapore, and Thailand also said they completed foreign exchange settlement trial linking traditional and tokenized systems.

#4920. Body Recomposition Basics: How to Lose Fat and Gain Muscle, According to a Doctor

Your body recomposition journey starts here.

Body recomposition is the fitness goal these days. If you’ve been hearing the term everywhere like I have, and thinking body recompo-what, you’re not alone.

So, what is body recomp? Whether you knew it or not, chances are, you’ve probably pursued it at some point. If you’ve ever set out to reduce body fat or build muscle, you’ve been working toward a body recomposition goal. When people say body recomp these days, they really mean simultaneously losing fat and building muscle, not just one or the other.

Meet the expert: Brittany Busse, MD, is the chief medical officer and cofounder of ViTel Health.

Unlike simply losing weight, this approach isn’t about the number on the scale; it’s about improving the ratio of fat to muscle in your body for better health, performance, and aesthetics. (Oftentimes, when people talk about wanting to look "toned," they're really talking about body recomp, since you need low amounts of body fat to see the muscle you've built up.)

And, while body recomposition is completely possible, it can be a little more technical than other fitness goals. Here are the core things you need to know to get started on your body recomp journey.

Get started with our exclusive body recomp guide.

First: a quick refresher. Body composition refers to a percentage breakdown of how much body fat, lean mass (that is, muscle!), and bone you've got on your body. Body recomposition is the process through which you change that breakdown.

These are the five most important things to keep in mind when trying to make that happen.

At the most basic level, losing fat requires a calorie deficit; you need to burn more than you consume. Working with a nutritionist or doctor, you can determine exactly what this means for you, but for body recomposition, it's only a slight deficit that you should be shooting for. We’re talking 250 to 500 calories max.

Keep in mind: “Weight loss should not be confused with fat loss,” Brittany Busse, MD, the chief medical officer and cofounder of ViTel Health previously told Women's Health. “Much of weight loss can also be loss of muscle mass.”

And, you don't want to lose muscle mass, particularly if your goal is body recomp. That’s why protein is critical, Dr. Busse says—but it’s just one piece of the puzzle. Tracking all three macros (protein, carbs, and fat) can go a long way in helping you stay full, energized, and strong while pursuing body recomp.

GET MORE INFO ABOUT COUNTING MACROS FOR BODY RECOMP WITH THE WH+ PDF.

Lifting is nonnegotiable. “People should weight train at least three times a week,” Dr. Busse said. “Weight training will build muscle mass, which will inevitably lead to improved metabolic health and fat loss.”

Keep up your cardio, too. But, if you’re a HIIT addict, you may want to try slowing things down. “Zone 2 cardio is the most effective way to burn fat while sparing muscle. This is exercising at a level where you can hold a ‘breathy’ conversation comfortably for 45-60 minutes,” Dr. Busse said. “Walking on an incline, cycling, and rucking are all examples of Zone 2 workouts,” she said.

It's hard to come up with a training plan all on your own, so relying on the expertise of trainers to create a program can help make sure you're working your muscles efficiently and effectively.

Women's Health+ has many body recomp-focused programs for people of all experience levels: the 4-Week Walking Plan, the 4-Week Strength Training Plan, the 4-Week Build & Burn Series (which allows you to follow along with dumbbell, barbell, or kettlebell-based workouts), and the Body Recomp Guide.

Age, hormones, and genetics all play a role in body composition, as does access to high-quality food and medical care. Not everyone has the same amount of time to spend exercising. So, take it easy on yourself, and if you can, get help and support as you work toward your goals.

#4919. You Can See Everything You Ever Want to See in a Movie in You Can See Everything

Nathan Fielder’s new Elizabeth Holmes documentary is three hours long. You’ll wish it went on for three more.

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

NATHAN FIELDER HAS become one of the greatest arbiters of what is—or isn’t—the truth. Fielder, whose mainstream career unofficially kicked off with his show Nathan for You, a dry, quasi-documentary, quasi-scripted, quasi-spoof of shows like Undercover Boss, has found a way to level up with each project he’s made over the course of his still relatively short career, each step of the way inviting audiences to not only question the reality of what he’s bringing to the screen, but their own stances and ways of thinking about things broadly.

The road for Fielder has included HBO’s The Rehearsal (another often surreal, often Lynchian project that presents as real, but on a subtextual level asks viewers to question whether any of what he’s depicting was really happening as it was shown) and The Curse, a Showtime/Paramount+ series that he starred in and co-created alongside Emma Stone and Benny Safdie. That show was, surprise, surprise, incredibly thoughtful, layered, and, ultimately, surreal when it comes to its underlying themes of sincerity and intention.

In a way, all of this has led Fielder to his latest project, the new A24 documentary You Can See Everything. The subject is a fitting one for Fielder: Elizabeth Holmes, the former Theranos CEO and convicted fraudster who was the subject of books (Bad Blood) and television shows (The Dropout) about her misdeeds. It makes total sense that someone famous for skirting the truth would be of interest for Fielder, a creator who has now spent so much time examining not only the truth, but what audiences might accept as the truth even given some reason not to.

In 2022, Holmes was sentenced to 11 years and 3 months in federal prison. That’s where You Can See Everything comes in: Holmes and her partner Billy Evans invited Fielder (and a film crew, led by co-director Lance Oppenheim) to join them in a home they were renting for complete access during the 34 days before she reported to federal prison in Bryan, Texas, in May 2023. And the film begins there.

And, quite frankly, if you’re considering seeing You Can See Everything, it’s best to leave it there. Fielder gets the access he was promised in the movie, but the joy of the film isn’t only in this exclusive vision of such a notable figure, but how an artist with such a relationship to the truth engages with someone who so notably has, seemingly, bent it. We also get to see Holmes and Evans shot as human beings, removed from any of the prior media circuses that have surrounded them. Fielder and Oppenheim put a fair camera to everything and let the camera do what was promised: See everything.

You Can See Everything has been one of the best-reviewed films of the year, and it lives up to the billing. Just when you think you understand what’s happening and what’s going to happen, you’ll be quickly proven wrong. Just when you think you have a handle on who someone is and what they’re all about… you’ll quickly be proven wrong. The movie is three hours long, which, of course, we know, seems daunting. But by the time it ends, you’ll wish it was going on for three hours more.

Below, we answer some of your questions about You Can See Everything—without spoiling any of the movie’s major twists or turns.

You Can See Everything is now available to watch at home. You can purchase it on Apple TV and rent it on Prime Video—and we suggest doing whichever of those you prefer.

You Can See Everything is, in essence, two movies in one. The first half of the movie is what the trailer and promotional materials for the movie billed: Nathan Fielder joins Elizabeth Holmes (and her new husband Billy Evans) in a home they rented for the 34 days before she reported to federal prison in 2023. This proves to be just as compelling as you’d imagine, as Holmes and Evans are both completely idiosyncratic characters. Moments like when Fielder shows Holmes Abbott and Costello’s “Who’s on First” bit are instant classics.

Eventually Holmes reports to prison in Bryan, Texas, and the movie is not even halfway over. It’s at this point that your eyebrow should raise, and you do the ‘leaning forward in seat’ meme—because this is when You Can See Everything gets truly wild. The timeline jumps forward two hours, and Nathan Fielder gets up to some of his mind-bending, Rehearsal-type business. At this point, we see some people’s true colors, and also meet some other unexpected guests and surprises in the movie. This second part of the movie is what will blow your mind, and leave you thinking long after the credits begin to roll.

You Can See Everything should be an absolute lock for a number of Oscar nominations, including Best Picture. And it should be a strong contender in one of the acting categories for one person whose appearance we will not be spoiling in this story.

Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim are the co-directors of You Can See Everything, and both have been key figures in American film and television culture for the last decade.

Fielder is a Canadian-born actor and director (and childhood friend of Seth Rogen) who rose to fame as the creator and star of Comedy Central’s Nathan for You. He’s dabbled in acting here and there—including a role as a limo driver in Rogen’s underrated holiday comedy The Night Before and in the sensational limited series The Curse—but his real calling has come in mind-bending documentary/comedy series like The Rehearsal. In season 2 of The Rehearsal, for example, Fielder actually got his pilot’s license while exploring the aviation industry. (And that was filmed between part 1 and part 2 of You Can See Everything, which is just bananas.)

Oppenheim, who is only 30, has also established himself as one of the best documentarians in the business. His movies Some Kind of Heaven and Spermworld along with his HBO series Ren Faire are deeply layered portrayals of very real people in very real situations; he shoots these documentaries in styles completely different from anyone else, though, lighting them like cinematic spectacles rather than what you probably think of as a documentary in your mind. (Some of the cinematography in You Can See Everything is unbelievably beautiful.)

Primetime, A24’s film about Chris Hansen and To Catch a Predator that came out last month and starred Robert Pattinson, Skyler Gisondo, and Merritt Wever, was Oppenheim’s scripted feature debut.

It probably helps to have information on Elizabeth Holmes’s case—which we recommend getting from any number of sources: The Dropout was the name of the Hulu series that starred Amanda Seyfried as Holmes, but it was also a well-researched and reported podcast that served as the show’s basis. There’s also an HBO documentary called The Inventor and a book called Bad Blood. Any of this would make for a good source for the crimes Holmes was accused of committing. The movie also includes a very brief recap of her case in the early going—not exhaustive, but enough to get the idea.

It does also make sense to have an idea of who Fielder is, what he does, and how he engages with his subjects. We recommend HBO’s The Rehearsal for that, but it’s not 100 percent necessary to enjoy and appreciate the film.

That’s the question, isn’t it? You Can See Everything explores the idea of truth, lies, perspective, and even documentary filmmaking itself. If it makes the most sense to you to take all of You Can See Everything at face value, then please go for it. If you feel the need to question everything, well, that’s okay too. That’s what makes Fielder’s work so unique and so immersive—you can think about it about 100 different ways, and no understanding or interpretation is wrong. It’s set up to feel like a kaleidoscope. You can understand something one way, but maybe something pops up, and suddenly you can’t think about it that way anymore. That’s the point—and that’s what you’ll think about long after the credits roll.
